purpose: Check the edges of the CDM triple KG (outputs/results/kg_2026-11-04) against curated knowledge graphs, independent of the source paper: is the association known anywhere in the reference? Absence is reported as NOT_IN_REFERENCE, never as an error.

bugsigdb.pairs: signature taxa x Condition (all signatures with a direction)

node_type: type_cleaned from the cleaned layer, falling back to the CDM type

edge_types.gene_disease: PROTEIN, DNA_RNA or GENOMICS with DISEASE
edge_types.chemical_gene: CHEMICAL with PROTEIN, DNA_RNA or GENOMICS

resolution.taxon: node ontology_id NCBITaxon, else exact unique name in NCBI Taxonomy names.dmp; matched at the same ID or after lifting both sides to genus
resolution.disease: MeSH ID from the node ontology_id, else exact name or synonym in CTD_diseases (MEDIC). Disbiome and BugSigDB diseases are mapped the same way; a disease also matches on identical normalised name
resolution.chemical: MeSH ID from the node ontology_id, else exact name or synonym in CTD_chemicals
resolution.gene: human gene_info symbol or synonym (upper case, at least 3 characters), unique

primary: per edge type: share of resolved edges whose pair is in at least one reference, with chance
secondary: the same for kept vs dropped by the DeepSeek cleaning (Newcombe interval of the difference)
the same for edges whose sentence supports the original label (evidence check A = Y) vs not

chance: share of all cross pairs (distinct resolved entities of one side x the other side, within the edge type) that are in the reference
limitations_stated_in_advance: Reference KGs are incomplete; absence is not error.
Name matching can map a generic label to a specific concept; resolution methods are reported.
Reference support shows that an association is known, not that the triple's paper states it or that the direction is right.
